message.content: The largest planet that has been observed so far is the protoplanet **HD 100546 b**. It orbits the young star HD 100546 and has a radius roughly 2½–3 times that of Jupiter (about 30–35 R⊕). Because it is still forming, its exact size and mass are uncertain, but it remains the biggest planetary‑mass object detected to date.
